_meta.indication: Diagnostic PET imaging of the myocardium under rest or pharmacologic stress conditions to evaluate myocardial perfusion in patients with suspected or existing coronary artery disease

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Descriptive, prospective, blinded image interpretation study (Demer et al., Circulation 1989) comparing Ammonia N 13 and Rubidium 82 PET to coronary angiography
pivotal_trials.nct: Not reported (NDA based on published literature; no new clinical trial)
pivotal_trials.phase: Not applicable; efficacy based on published literature, no definitive randomized controlled trials
pivotal_trials.design: Descriptive, prospective, blinded image interpretation study comparing PET perfusion defect severity to stenosis flow reserve determined by coronary angiography
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with known or suspected coronary artery disease
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Evaluation of PET defect severity relative to stenosis flow reserve (SFR)
pivotal_trials.n: N=111 (Ammonia N 13) and N=82 (Rubidium 82); 193 patients total in the referenced study
pivotal_trials.result: With increasing impairment of flow reserve, PET defect severity increased; a PET defect score of 2 or higher was positively correlated with flow reserve impairment (SFR<3)

key_safety: No adverse reactions have been reported for Ammonia N 13 Injection based on review of the literature, publicly available reference sources, and adverse drug reaction reporting systems; principal risk is radiation exposure
target_moa: Radiolabeled analog of ammonia; after IV injection it is extracted from blood in the coronary capillaries into myocardial cells where it is metabolized to glutamine N 13 and retained, allowing PET imaging of myocardial perfusion

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held; listed as 'None' / Not applicable

summary.text: NDA 22-119 was submitted under section 505(b)(2) of the FD&C Act by the Feinstein Institute, containing no new primary clinical data but relying on the FDA's prior literature-based finding of safety and effectiveness for PET drugs (FR March 10, 2000); it was approved with no advisory committee meeting and no required Phase 4 commitments.

citations.quote: Please refer to your new drug application (NDA) dated October 16, 2006, received October 25, 2006, submitted pursuant to section 505(b)(2) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act for Ammonia N 13 Injection.
It contained no primary clinical data, but rather reference to the Agency's review of safety and effectiveness
No recommendations for phase 4 commitments are being made at this time.
